subject: Biotechnology
title: Knockout Mice
description: Learn Knockout Mice in one minute.

hook.text: Delete one gene from a mouse and see what breaks — knockout mice reveal what every gene actually does.

buildup.text: Homologous recombination replaces a gene with a disrupted copy in embryonic stem cells — then the mouse grows.

discovery.text: The p53 knockout mouse develops cancer at alarming rates — proving p53 is a critical tumor suppressor.

twist.text: Some knockouts have no visible effect — redundant genes compensate, hiding the deleted gene's role.

climax.text: Capecchi, Evans, and Smithies won the 2007 Nobel Prize — knockout technology transformed medical research.

punchline.text: Delete a gene, watch what happens — reverse engineering life.

quiz.question: What is a knockout mouse?
options: A mouse that has been trained to respond to specific stimuli
A mouse with a specific gene intentionally disabled to study its function
A mouse bred to be resistant to all known diseases

details.summary: Knockout mice are genetically engineered to have specific genes permanently inactivated, revealing each gene's function through the resulting phenotype. They are the primary model for understanding mammalian gene function and have contributed to thousands of disease research breakthroughs.
details.whyItMatters: Knockout mice earned the 2007 Nobel Prize because they transformed our understanding of gene function. By observing what happens when a gene is missing, researchers discovered the roles of genes in cancer, immunity, development, and countless other
takeaways: Knockout mice have specific genes permanently disabled to study gene function
The technology earned the 2007 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine
CRISPR has dramatically accelerated and simplified knockout mouse production

faq.question: How are knockout mice created?
faq.answer: Traditionally, a targeting vector replaces the gene with a selectable marker in embryonic stem cells. ES cells are injected into blastocysts to create chimeric mice, which are bred to produce fully knockout progeny.

faq.question: Why are mice used instead of other animals for gene knockouts?
faq.answer: Mouse genetics is well-characterized with a fully sequenced genome sharing 85 percent of protein-coding genes with humans. Mice breed quickly with large litters, are economical to house, and well-established protocols enable genetic manipulation. No other mammalian model offers this combination.
